subject.title: [Feature]: muteKeywords channel config — drop messages matching keyword/regex list before agent dispatch

question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in per-channel literal/regex inbound content filter for Slack and Discord, and what shared contract should it use?
rationale: This adds a new config/API surface and intentional silent message drops on channel hot paths, so automation cannot choose the product semantics safely.

options.title: Define a shared channel filter contract
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify the field name, match semantics, regex safety, logging, history behavior, and per-plugin rollout.

options.title: Narrow to one channel first
options.body: Accept the idea only for one owner plugin, such as Slack, and require a follow-up decision before copying it to Discord or other channels.

options.title: Decline built-in keyword muting
options.body: Close or mark not planned if maintainers prefer operators to solve this outside OpenClaw or through channel-specific bot configuration.

recommendation.title: Define a shared channel filter contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify the field name, match semantics, regex safety, logging, history behavior, and per-plugin rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent channel/config work and adjacent Slack hardening make this the best available routing candidate for the product/API decision.
